# Fish Catcher

> Fish Catcher is a free, open-source (MIT) browser extension that warns you, in plain language, when a website looks like phishing or a scam. It never blocks a page, and its default checks run entirely on your device, so nothing about the pages you visit is sent anywhere.

## What it is

- A Manifest V3 browser extension for Chrome, Brave, Edge, Opera, and Firefox.
- Built for non-technical users. It shows a risk color and explains why in a sentence or two.
- Risk colors: green (no suspicious signs), yellow (a little unusual), orange (several indicators), red (strong signs of a fake).
- Local-first and private by default: no account, no tracking, no server. Optional online features are off until you turn them on.

## What it detects

- Brand impersonation: misspelled or look-alike domains and homoglyph tricks.
- URL tricks: raw IP addresses, the @ trick, high-abuse domain endings, long subdomain chains, unencrypted logins, digit-heavy names.
- Known-bad lists: a bundled blocklist plus a daily community feed (Phishing.Database, URLhaus by abuse.ch, and OpenPhish), matched on your device.
- Page checks: a login form on a site it does not know, and device-code sign-in scams.
- On-device model: spots the random, computer-generated addresses fresh phishing uses.
- AiTM (adversary-in-the-middle): a sign-in or code prompt on a site whose address does not match the brand it imitates.
- Scam packs: pages asking for a crypto wallet recovery phrase or private key, and fake tech-support "call this number" pages.
- QR codes: reads the link inside a QR image on your device before you trust it.
- Optional layers (off by default): Google Safe Browsing (with your own free key) and an RDAP domain-age check.

## Accuracy

- Measured false-positive rate: 0.005% (5 warnings at high, 0 at critical) across 100,000 legitimate domains from the Majestic Million, as of 2026-08-11.
- The audit is reproducible: run `node scripts/fp-audit.mjs` in the source repository. It prints every domain it flagged.

## Facts

- License: MIT (free and open source).
- Privacy: on-device by default; nothing about your browsing leaves your browser unless you enable an optional online feature, and each sends only the one domain it needs.
- Source (extension): https://github.com/Topurrra/fishcatcher
- Threat registry: https://github.com/Topurrra/fishcatcher-registry
- Website: https://fishcatcher.dev
